WITH cleaned_weather AS (
    -- Remove duplicates by keeping only one record per location_id and date
    -- Use the record with the most complete data (prioritize non-null values)
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (location_id, date)
        location_id,
        date,
        max_temp_c,
        min_temp_c,
        avg_temp_c
    FROM daily_weather
    WHERE 
        -- Filter out NULL temperature values
        max_temp_c IS NOT NULL 
        AND min_temp_c IS NOT NULL 
        AND avg_temp_c IS NOT NULL
        -- Filter out unreasonable temperature values (data quality check)
        AND max_temp_c BETWEEN -100 AND 60
        AND min_temp_c BETWEEN -100 AND 60
        AND avg_temp_c BETWEEN -100 AND 60
        -- Ensure logical consistency: min <= avg <= max
        AND min_temp_c <= avg_temp_c 
        AND avg_temp_c <= max_temp_c
    ORDER BY 
        location_id, 
        date,
        -- Prioritize records with more complete data in case of duplicates
        (CASE WHEN max_temp_c IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
         CASE WHEN min_temp_c IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
         CASE WHEN avg_temp_c IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC
)
SELECT 
    l.name AS location_name,
    l.country,
    TO_CHAR(cw.date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(cw.avg_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS avg_temperature,
    ROUND(MIN(cw.min_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS min_temperature,
    ROUND(MAX(cw.max_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS max_temperature,
    COUNT(*) AS days_with_data
FROM cleaned_weather cw
INNER JOIN locations l ON cw.location_id = l.location_id
GROUP BY 
    l.location_id,
    l.name,
    l.country,
    TO_CHAR(cw.date, 'YYYY-MM')
ORDER BY 
    l.name,
    month;
